name: The Davis household at the American
head: davis_t_o

arrival.note: Not_later_than precision on the last day of the month in which his paper first appeared. He was in Chicago by then because his paper was; when he came is not stated, and this is the one household in the parcel where the arrival gate is doing real work rather than waving a decade-old date through.

reason_for_coming.value: To start a second newspaper in the boom
reason_for_coming.note: The town's population roughly quadrupled between the Democrat's founding and his own; a second paper is the obvious commercial reading and is not stated.

present_on_scene_date.note: Publishing at Chicago in June 1835 and through the year - the American of 15 August 1835 counting the town's eight taverns, and of 10 October 1835 tabulating the land office's takings, are both quoted by Andreas.

persons.name: T. O. Davis

occupation.note: Founder and publisher of the Chicago American, the town's second newspaper, from June 1835.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED RESIDENT OF THE SCENE MONTH ITSELF - the American's first issue belongs to June 1835, weeks before 1 July, which makes this one of only three households in the parcel whose Chicago presence is fixed by an event inside the scene season. data/structures/chicago_american_office.json already carries him. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “T. O. Davis,” (f1839_v0104, printed page 42, ward 1, voting for John H. Kinzie). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Davis' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins T. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

resident_research.evidence_for: Independent of the post office in 1840 census, civic rolls, directories and more.
resident_research.notes: Candidate facts remain unasserted until a source bridges the candidate to the historical record by more than name similarity.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

research_note: THE NEWEST ARRIVAL IN THE PARCEL, and the one whose paper this project quotes most often for the state of the town in the scene year. A NOTE FOR ANY LATER PARCEL: the Chicago American of 1835-36 is the single most valuable unfetched source for this programme. Andreas quotes its advertisements by name and date - Frederick Thomas's drug and paint store of 8 June 1835, John Davis of the Steamboat Hotel among its first patrons, W. H. and A. F. Clarke's new drug store of 11 November 1835 - and every such advertisement is a documented resident with a trade and often an address, in the scene year rather than nineteen months before it.
